Choose a cutoff: use all 2026/27 matches completed by a stated date. For each team, record how many matches it has played; postponed fixtures can mean those counts differ.

Recreate that same point in past seasons: for example, take each historical season after each team has played a similar number of matches. Use statistics available by that point as predictors and final season points as the target.

Backtest before forecasting: train on earlier seasons, validate your choices on a later season, and evaluate on a held-out season at the same early-season stage. This tests whether your approach could have made a useful forecast before you apply it to 2026/27.

Fit your simple GAM: predict final points from a small number of early-season summaries, then sort predicted points to produce the table. Compare it with a simple baseline, such as projecting current points per game over a full season.

Show how forecasts change: if time permits, repeat the historical backtest at more than one cutoff. That lets you show whether predictions improve as more matches are played.



## Idea

To start with, I have the broad idea of firstly, recording and predicting the total goals at the end of the season of each team (time dependent). 
Through this I want the model to follow certain conditions(can add this at the end): (this can be an if else statement)
- the team with most points at the end ends up top and record the rest of the list  depending on the number of points of the team at time t=end
- we also want the team to record the total number of goals of each team at the end of the season to calculate its goal difference(this is the total goals scored across the season minus the total goals conceded). We want the top team to have the lasrgest number of goal difference (max(gd)).
-if two teams finish with same number of points and goal difference, then the model should simulate a match between the two top teams and the winner comes up as top. (if there are more than two teams in this position they they should all play eachother until we get another ranking of who's the winnner until convergence)

## Time dependent observations

Given a set of data, we want to determine the ranking at the end of the season with data that starts at the beginning of the season. 
Train/Validation split will be each year at random???
  



Instead of directly wanting to predict the rank by giving two conditions (i.e. points and the GD) I can put these two together byt coding something along the lines of:
- Record the total number of goals of each team
eg.

match: arsenal v everton ->  if Arsenal goals > Everton goals => Everton loses (pt=0) and Arsenal (pt=3)
                         ->  elif Arsenal goals = Everton goals => draw so Everton(pt=1) and Arsenal (pt=1)
                         ->  else Arsenal goals < Everton goals => Everton wins (pt=3) and Arsenal (pt=3)
To use the total number goals of goals:

match: arsenal v everton ->  if (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Arsenal > (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Everton => Everton loses (pt=0) and Arsenal (pt=3)
                         ->  elif (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Arsenal = (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Everton => draw so Everton(pt=1) and Arsenal (pt=1)
                         ->  else (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Arsenal  < (Total number of goals before match - total number of goals after match)Everton  => Everton wins (pt=3) and Arsenal (pt=3)

Ranking will consiste of teams with highest number of points 

##Rank Regression

As with least squares, the goal of rank-based regression is to estimate the vector of coefficients, $\mathbf{\beta}$, of a general linear model of the form:
$$y_i = \alpha+\mathbf{x}^T_i \beta +e_i \ \text{for i=1,...n (1)} $$
where $y_i$ is the response variable, $\mathbf{x}_i$ is the vector of explanatory variables, $\alpha$ is the intercept parameter, and $e_i$ is the error term.

## Predicting c(Goals scored, goals conceded, points) for each team

First we look at the 2014/15 - 2024/25 training set. Here we have the following teams overall:
```{r}
train_teams<-unique(c(train_data$HomeTeam, train_data$AwayTeam))
length(train_teams)
```
```{r}
intersect(train_teams, unique(c(test_data$HomeTeam, test_data$AwayTeam)))
```
This tells us that from the train data set we have all the teams data from our test set which is great as this gives us more information for all of our observations.
```{r}
intersect(train_teams, unique(c(prediction_data$HomeTeam, prediction_data$AwayTeam)))
```
On the other hand, for our prediction dataset we do not have information for all the teams. We will expland on this when we get to the point in which we want to make the prediction.

```{r}
# Convert the match date and identify each season by its starting year

train_data$Date <- as.Date(as.character(train_data$Date), format = "%d/%m/%Y")

train_data$SeasonStart <- as.integer(format(train_data$Date, "%Y")) 

before_july <- as.integer(format(train_data$Date, "%m")) < 7

train_data$SeasonStart[before_july] <- train_data$SeasonStart[before_july] - 1



outcome_columns <- c("FTHG", "FTAG", "HG", "AG", "Date", "SeasonStart") #response variable

predictor_columns <- setdiff(names(train_data), outcome_columns)
predictor_columns <- setdiff(predictor_columns,c("HomeTeam", "AwayTeam", "FTR", "HS", "HTPA")) #variables CAN SIMPLIFY THIS


# Turn text columns into factors, keeping consistent levels across seasons
text_columns <- names(train_data)[sapply(train_data, is.character)] #names the text columns in the dataset
train_data[text_columns] <- lapply(train_data[text_columns], factor) #applies factor() to the text columns



# Store predicted tables here, one for each test season
season_tables <- list()

# Test each season using only seasons before it for training IS THE YEAR RANGE CORRECT??????
for (year in 2015:2024) {

  training_seasons <- train_data[train_data$SeasonStart < year, ] #trains the model with data from previous year
  test_season <- train_data[train_data$SeasonStart == year, ] #tests the model with data of selected year
  
  if (nrow(training_seasons) == 0 || nrow(test_season) == 0) {
    next
  }

#I CAN REWRITE THE FOLLOWING IN SIMPLER WORDS:
  home_formula <- reformulate(predictor_columns, response = "FTHG") # creates a formula such as FTHG~., variables = predictor_columns
  away_formula <- reformulate(predictor_columns, response = "FTAG") # creates a formula such as FTHG~., variables = predictor_columns

  home_model <- glm(home_formula, data = training_seasons, family = poisson)
  away_model <- glm(away_formula, data = training_seasons, family = poisson)

  # Predict the held-out season's match goals : WRITE THIS IN MATHEMATICS
  test_season$PredHomeGoals <- round(predict(home_model, newdata = test_season, type = "response")) # predicting Y_homegoals

  test_season$PredAwayGoals <- round(predict(away_model, newdata = test_season, type = "response")) # predicting Y_awaygoals

  # Turn the predicted scores into points and goals for each team
  
  home_table <- data.frame(Team = test_season$HomeTeam,Points = ifelse(test_season$PredHomeGoals > test_season$PredAwayGoals,
                                                                       3,
                                                                       ifelse(test_season$PredHomeGoals == test_season$PredAwayGoals,
                                                                              1,
                                                                              0)),
                            GF = test_season$PredHomeGoals, GA = test_season$PredAwayGoals) #GF = goals home, GA= goals away

  away_table <- data.frame(Team = test_season$AwayTeam,Points = ifelse(test_season$PredAwayGoals > test_season$PredHomeGoals,
                                                                       3,
                                                                       ifelse(test_season$PredAwayGoals == test_season$PredHomeGoals,
                                                                              1,
                                                                              0)),
                            GF = test_season$PredAwayGoals, GA = test_season$PredHomeGoals)
  

  all_team_matches <- rbind(home_table, away_table)
  table <- aggregate(cbind(Points, GF, GA) ~ Team, data = all_team_matches, sum) # splits the data into subsets, computes summary statistics for each, and returns the result in a convenient form?? LOOK THIS FUNCTION UP

  table$GD <- table$GF - table$GA  #calculating goal difference
  table <- table[order(-table$Points, -table$GD, -table$GF), ] #adding the points, gd and gf in increasing order onto the table
  table$Position <- seq_len(nrow(table)) # labels the position as increasing order from data in the table
  table <- table[c("Position", "Team", "Points", "GF", "GA", "GD")]

  season_tables[[as.character(year)]] <- table
}



# View the predicted table for the 2024/25 test season
season_tables[["2024"]]
```
